content.value:
SolversLib provides Motor and MotorEx wrappers.

Motor wraps DcMotor with run modes and encoder utilities.

MotorEx extends Motor using DcMotorEx, with better velocity control, corrected velocity (fixes overflow bugs), and power caching.

Both are in com.seattlesolvers.solverslib.hardware.motors.

Declare a private MotorEx field.

In initialize(), create it with: motor = new MotorEx(hardwareMap, "front_left_motor"). That's it — no separate hardwareMap.get() call needed.

MotorEx gets the DcMotorEx from the hardware map internally.

MotorEx has three RunModes.

RawPower is the default — motor.set(0.5) sets 50% voltage, same as DcMotor.setPower().

VelocityControl uses encoder feedback and feedforward to hold a target speed.

PositionControl drives to a target encoder position.

Set the mode with motor.setRunMode(Motor.RunMode.VelocityControl).

We will touch on PID and feedforward tuning in Module 5: Control & Tuning.

Set the run mode to VelocityControl.

Set velocity PID coefficients: motor.setVeloCoefficients(0.05, 0.01, 0.31).

Set feedforward: motor.setFeedforwardCoefficients(0.92, 0.47).

Then schedule a SequentialCommandGroup: InstantCommand that calls motor.set(0.5) (50% of max velocity), WaitCommand(2000), InstantCommand that calls motor.set(0).

The motor holds constant speed regardless of battery level. Tuning these coefficients is covered in Module 5: Control & Tuning.

MotorEx has a nested Encoder class accessed via motor.encoder.

Reset with motor.resetEncoder() — this uses an offset internally so the motor doesn't need to stop.

Get position with motor.getCurrentPosition().

Get velocity with motor.getVelocity() (corrected, overflow-safe).

You can also set the encoder to use another motor's encoder: motor.encoder = otherMotor.encoder.

motor.setInverted(true) to reverse direction.

motor.setZeroPowerBehavior(Motor.ZeroPowerBehavior.BRAKE) to brake or float when stopped.

motor.setCachingTolerance(0.01) for power caching on MotorEx — skips writes if the power change is below the threshold.

motor.motor gives you the underlying DcMotor if needed.

motor.stopAndResetEncoder() for a hardware-level reset.
